examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of a Quadrilateral
examples.problem:
Rounded to the nearest integer, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946476/assets/bc9f32a9c0e8b042498a72e808a29274bd505e786d8ec43d0e0bc9888fdf6e44.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADC$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946476/assets/acd2e923a65d0821cd59ed8b8274ceb5fc38def896467e37c8b1d454f958699e.png)

 First, we find the area for $\triangle ABC,$ and get
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABC} & =\frac{1}{2}(42)(35)\operatorname{sin}⁡{36}^{∘} \\  & =735\operatorname{sin}⁡{36}^{∘} \\  & ≈432.022\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Now we find the area for $\triangle ADC,$ and get
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ADC} & =\frac{1}{2}(20)(18)\operatorname{sin}⁡{80}^{∘} \\  & =180\operatorname{sin}⁡{80}^{∘} \\  & ≈177.265\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD.$ We get
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & ={A}_{ABC}+{A}_{ADC} \\  & =432.022+177.265 \\  & ≈609\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, to the nearest integer, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $609.$

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2}{\text{cm}}^{2}.$ Then,  $AC=${{field-1}} $\text{cm}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=10\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={120}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 10\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\ \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 10\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\ \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2} & =5b\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ 25\cancel{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} & =5b\cdot \cancel{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \\ 5b & =25 \\ b & =5\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=5\,\text{ cm}.$
